title: Born of the Virgin (CCC 496–507)
hookLine: the Church professes Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit without a human father

lines: THE HOLY GHOST SHALL COME UPON THEE.
cards: A virgin in Nazareth, betrothed to a man named Joseph, has just been told she will have a son, that he will be great, and called the Son of the most High. Luke gives her one question, and it's a practical one.
In the Douay-Rheims: "How shall this be done, because I know not man?" She isn't asking for a sign. She's asking how.
And the angel's answer is the center of today: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the most High shall overshadow thee."
The Apostles' Creed folds that whole scene into a few words: born of the Virgin Mary.

teach.h: CONCEIVED BY THE HOLY SPIRIT ALONE.
teach.b: The Church confesses, the Catechism says, that Jesus was conceived solely by the power of the Holy Spirit in the womb of the Virgin Mary, with no human father.

teach.h: LUKE FROM MARY'S SIDE, MATTHEW JOSEPH'S.
teach.b: Luke tells it from Mary's side; Matthew from Joseph's. In Matthew, Joseph finds Mary with child and, being a just man, plans to send her away quietly.
Then an angel in a dream tells him that what is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost, and he takes her home as his wife. The Catechism is honest that this isn't an easy teaching.
People have objected; some have called it a legend.
Its reply is not a proof: the Gospels present it as God's own work, beyond human understanding, whose meaning opens up only to faith. What does it mean, in Catholic teaching?
First, the beginning is God's: Jesus has only God as his Father. Second, something new is starting: the Catechism calls Jesus the new Adam, the start of a new creation.
Third, it's a sign for everyone else, a new birth by the Spirit, which Catholics connect with baptism.
Day seventy-nine was the Immaculate Conception; this is a different teaching. The virginal conception is about how Jesus was conceived.
The Immaculate Conception is about Mary herself, kept free from original sin from the first moment of her own life.

teach.h: BE IT DONE TO ME ACCORDING TO THY WORD.
teach.b: And Mary's last line in Luke's scene is the one the Angelus repeats: "Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word."

how: Catholics profess the virginal conception in the Creed at Mass, and some pray the Angelus, a short prayer on the Annunciation said traditionally at morning, noon and evening.

in Luke, Mary asks the angel how this can happen
"How shall this be done, because I know not man?"
the Catechism offers a proof of the virginal conception
it says the Gospels present it as God's work, and that its meaning opens to faith.

games.q: you're Joseph, a just man. Mary, your betrothed, is with child, and it isn't yours. what do you do?
o: act as if nothing has happened
games.why: Matthew says he planned to send her away privately. then an angel in a dream told him the child was of the Holy Ghost, and he took Mary as his wife.

practice: The Angelus, an old Catholic prayer by tradition said when a church bell rings, walks through this very scene: the angel's message, Mary's answer, and the Word made flesh, with a Hail Mary between.

If you pray and know it, pray it now, slowly. If you don't, stay with Mary's answer instead, be it done to me according to thy word, and notice how it feels to say yes to something you can't fully see.

wordCard.voice: Virginal conception. Jesus conceived by the Holy Spirit, with no human father; not the Immaculate Conception. Today's word.
